situation: An employer hiring customer service agents for a new team through panel interviews.
complication: There are more screened candidates than free interview hours, and many booked candidates do not attend.
key_question: How should the panel interviews be scheduled so every screened candidate is seen in time?

titles.situation: Screened candidates outnumber free interview hours.
titles.options: Two ways to fit the interviews in.
titles.recommendation: Add panel hours and confirm every booking with a reminder.
titles.roadmap: Book interviews, run them, then report attendance.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the interviews ran well.
titles.risks: The main risk is candidates dropping out while they wait.

options.name: More hours and reminders

options.name: Book in screening order

recommendation.rationale: It gives all [F2] candidates a slot and protects panel time from no-shows; the manager approves every booking and message and decides who is hired.

work.title: Panel interview invitation
work.for: Screened candidates, email for the customer service manager to approve before sending
body: Hello, thank you for speaking with us. We would like to invite you to a panel interview for the customer service agent role.
The interview lasts about an hour, with two of our team managers. You will talk through how you help customers and work through a short example call together.
Please reply with your choice of the slots below, or tell us if none of them work and we will find another time.
We will send a reminder the day before. If your plans change, just reply to this email so we can offer the slot to someone else.
We look forward to meeting you. The recruiting team.
